:::{#thm-block-quadratic}
#### The quadratic form of a block matrix

Let $\matr{X}$ be the symmetric $(k + m) \times (k + m)$ matrix with blocks

$$
\matr{X} = \begin{bmatrix} \underbrace{\matr{A}}_{k \times k} & \underbrace{\matr{B}}_{k \times m} \\ \underbrace{\tp{\matr{B}}}_{m \times k} & \underbrace{\matr{C}}_{m \times m} \end{bmatrix},
$$

with $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{C}$ symmetric,
and split $\vx \in \reals^{k + m}$ as $\vx = (\vecf{u}, \vecf{w})$
with $\vecf{u} \in \reals^k$ its first $k$ entries and $\vecf{w} \in \reals^m$ the rest.
Then

$$
\tp{\vx} \matr{X} \vx
= \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} + 2\,\tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{B} \vecf{w} + \tp{\vecf{w}} \matr{C} \vecf{w},
$$

and if $\matr{A}$ is invertible, with $\matr{S} \eqdef \matr{C} - \tp{\matr{B}} \matr{A}^{-1} \matr{B}$
and $\vecf{z} \eqdef \vecf{u} + \matr{A}^{-1} \matr{B} \vecf{w}$,

$$
\tp{\vx} \matr{X} \vx = \tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{A} \vecf{z} + \tp{\vecf{w}} \matr{S} \vecf{w}.
$$

:::

::: proof

**The expansion.**
By @def-matvec-mult, entry $i \le k$ of $\matr{X} \vx$ is
$\sum_{j \le k} a_{ij} u_j + \sum_{j} b_{ij} w_j$,
and entry $k + i$ is $\sum_{j} (\tp{\matr{B}})_{ij} u_j + \sum_{j} c_{ij} w_j$,
so $\matr{X} \vx = (\matr{A} \vecf{u} + \matr{B} \vecf{w},\; \tp{\matr{B}} \vecf{u} + \matr{C} \vecf{w})$.
The dot product of $\vx = (\vecf{u}, \vecf{w})$ with it splits into the first $k$ and last $m$ terms:

$$
\ba
\tp{\vx} \matr{X} \vx
&= \vecf{u} \cdot (\matr{A} \vecf{u} + \matr{B} \vecf{w}) + \vecf{w} \cdot (\tp{\matr{B}} \vecf{u} + \matr{C} \vecf{w})
&& \text{(@def-dot-product, split the sum)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} + \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{B} \vecf{w} + \tp{\vecf{w}} \tp{\matr{B}} \vecf{u} + \tp{\vecf{w}} \matr{C} \vecf{w}
&& \text{(@thm-dot-linear)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} + 2\,\tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{B} \vecf{w} + \tp{\vecf{w}} \matr{C} \vecf{w}.
&& \text{(} \tp{\vecf{w}} \tp{\matr{B}} \vecf{u} = \tp{(\tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{B} \vecf{w})} \text{, a } 1 \times 1 \text{ matrix)}
\ea
$$

**Completing the square.**
Write $\vecf{d} \eqdef \matr{A}^{-1} \matr{B} \vecf{w}$, so $\vecf{z} = \vecf{u} + \vecf{d}$ and $\matr{A} \vecf{d} = \matr{B} \vecf{w}$.
$\matr{A}^{-1}$ is symmetric (@cor-inverse-symmetric). Then

$$
\ba
\tp{\vecf{z}} \matr{A} \vecf{z}
&= (\vecf{u} + \vecf{d}) \cdot (\matr{A} \vecf{u} + \matr{A} \vecf{d})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-distrib)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} + \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{d} + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{A} \vecf{d}
&& \text{(@thm-dot-linear, both slots)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} + 2\,\tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{d} + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{A} \vecf{d}
&& \text{(} \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} = \tp{(\tp{\vecf{u}} \tp{\matr{A}} \vecf{d})} = \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{d} \text{, } \matr{A} \text{ symmetric)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} + 2\,\tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{B} \vecf{w} + \tp{\vecf{d}} \matr{B} \vecf{w}
&& \text{(} \matr{A} \vecf{d} = \matr{B} \vecf{w} \text{, twice)}
\\
&= \tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{A} \vecf{u} + 2\,\tp{\vecf{u}} \matr{B} \vecf{w} + \tp{\vecf{w}}\,\tp{\matr{B}} \matr{A}^{-1} \matr{B} \vecf{w},
&& \text{(} \tp{\vecf{d}} = \tp{\vecf{w}} \tp{\matr{B}} \matr{A}^{-1} \text{, @thm-transpose-product)}
\ea
$$

and adding $\tp{\vecf{w}} \matr{S} \vecf{w} = \tp{\vecf{w}} \matr{C} \vecf{w} - \tp{\vecf{w}}\,\tp{\matr{B}} \matr{A}^{-1} \matr{B} \vecf{w}$
(@thm-scalar-matmul) gives the expansion of $\tp{\vx} \matr{X} \vx$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-block-quadratic}
#### The $2 \times 2$ case

For $\matr{X} = \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ b & c \end{bmatrix}$ ($k = m = 1$) and $a \ne 0$,
the theorem reads

$$
a x^2 + 2bxy + cy^2 = a\,\paren{x + \tfrac{b}{a}\,y}^2 + \paren{c - \tfrac{b^2}{a}}\,y^2,
$$

the familiar completing of the square.
With $a = c = 5$ and $b = 4$:
$5\,(x + 0.8\,y)^2 + 1.8\,y^2 = 5x^2 + 8xy + 3.2\,y^2 + 1.8\,y^2 = 5x^2 + 8xy + 5y^2$.

:::
